statement: Retention for sql_transactions, sql_transaction_participants and sql_write_operations. The first two are propagated, never deleted and scanned in full every second by the recovery sweep; sql_write_operations is write-only. The work is coupled to 2PC recovery, the release-census digest and settlement's row-absent refusal: a retired row must be distinguishable from a row that never existed wherever those owners decide on absence. The one-second full-table recovery scan is recorded as a load finding and bounded here or routed to its owner. Size L.

constraints.statement: No row deletion lands before the fresh-formation scenario holds three consecutive lab passes and CDC delivery stages 1-3 (solve/epics/operation-integrity-and-reliable-formation/cdc-delivery-design-note-2026-11-11.md) have landed.
One retention owner per table and one deletion path (R01, R11). Retention rides an existing reconcile trigger; it adds no timer.

A row is deleted only when it is terminal AND past its per-table horizon AND proven unreferenced by every dependency listed for its table (2PC recovery, the release-census digest, settlement and the partition participant store). Age and terminal status alone never authorize a delete.

Settlement refuses when the transaction row is absent. Retention must not turn that refusal into a wrong answer or make a retired transaction look unknown where the difference decides an outcome; any change to what absence means is an owner ruling recorded before sealing.

Deletes are guarded and idempotent (R14) and run in bounded batches paced under the cache-tombstone bound (30 s TTL, 1024 tombstones per table), at background priority, so that load slows retention and never breaks correctness (R12).

A propagated table is never expired by time inside apply: that bypasses CDC and leaves every cache stale. Its rows are deleted through the owner gateway so each delete is a replicated mutation with its CDC obligation.
sql_write_operations has writers and no reader in the census: name its reader and bound it, or delete the table and its writes (no-legacy rule).
The one-second full-table scan of the transaction tables is a load finding in its own right: its fix belongs to the recovery owner and may land before any deletion, since it does not delete rows.

A table moves out of class unbounded in solve/epics/system-table-retention/table-lifetimes.json only in the change that lands its retention owner, and the retained entry names that owner as file:symbol. The declaration is never edited to lower the epic metric ahead of the code.
The src/ changes land only behind an approving verification newer than the last attempt.
